theory.intro: A **budget** is a plan comparing **income** (money received) and **expenses** (money spent) over a set time period. It helps manage spending, meet commitments, and build savings.
facts: All amounts must be converted to the **same time period** ($1\text{ year} = 52\text{ weeks} = 26\text{ fortnights} = 12\text{ months}$).
**Fixed expenses** are recurring, non-negotiable costs with predictable amounts, such as rent, insurance, and loan repayments.
**Discretionary expenses** are flexible, non-essential spending choices that can be reduced, such as dining out and entertainment.
The financial position is given by $\text{Budget Balance} = \text{Total Income} - \text{Total Expenses}$.
A **surplus** occurs when income exceeds expenses, while a **deficit** occurs when expenses exceed income.
An **emergency fund** is a savings reserve covering $3$ to $6$ months of essential living expenses.
steps: Convert all income and expense items to the same time period
Categorise expenses into fixed and discretionary spending
Calculate total income and total expenses
Calculate the budget balance and determine if there is a surplus or deficit

foundation.question_text: A worker reviews their regular spending: Rent (\$350/week), Streaming subscriptions (\$18/month), Car loan repayment (\$220/fortnight), and Weekend dining out (\$80/week). Classify each expense as **fixed** or **discretionary**, and calculate their total weekly fixed expenses.
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{Rent: fixed (\$350/week)}$
$\text{Car loan: fixed (\$220/fortnight} = \$110\text{/week)}$
$\text{Streaming subscriptions: discretionary (\$18/month)}$
$\text{Weekend dining out: discretionary (\$80/week)}$
$\text{Total weekly fixed expenses} = \$350 + \$110$
$= \$460$

foundation.question_text: Liam earns a net salary of \$780 per week. Calculate his equivalent fortnightly, annual, and monthly income (using $52$ weeks per year).

Maya receives a net fortnightly income of \$1400. Her fortnightly living expenses total \$1180. Calculate Maya's annual budget balance and state whether she is in surplus (saving) or deficit (dissaving).
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Calculate total income and total expenses**
$\text{Annual income} = \$1400 \times 26 = \$36\,400$
$\text{Annual expenses} = \$1180 \times 26 = \$30\,680$
2. **Calculate the budget balance and determine if there is a surplus or deficit**
$\text{Budget balance} = \$36\,400 - \$30\,680$
$= \$5720\text{ surplus (saving)}$

foundation.question_text: A household has essential fixed living expenses of \$3200 per month. Calculate the target savings amount required to build an emergency fund covering $3$ months of living expenses.

Sam's monthly take-home pay is \$3600 and his total monthly expenses are \$3850 (consisting of \$2400 in fixed expenses and \$1450 in discretionary expenses). How much must Sam reduce his monthly discretionary spending to balance his budget ($\text{Balance} = \$0$)?
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{Monthly deficit} = \$3850 - \$3600 = \$250$
$\text{Required reduction in discretionary spending} = \$250$
$\text{New discretionary spending} = \$1450 - \$250$
$= \$1200$

development.question_text: An apprentice earns \$650 per week. His weekly expenses are: Board (fixed) \$180, Public transport (fixed) \$45, Phone plan (fixed) \$25, Gym membership (discretionary) \$15, Takeaway food (discretionary) \$70, and Video games (discretionary) \$35. Calculate his total annual fixed expenses and total annual discretionary expenses.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Weekly fixed expenses} = \$180 + \$45 + \$25 = \$250$
$\text{Annual fixed expenses} = \$250 \times 52 = \$13\,000$
$\text{Weekly discretionary expenses} = \$15 + \$70 + \$35 = \$120$
$\text{Annual discretionary expenses} = \$120 \times 52 = \$6240$

development.question_text: Daniel is comparing two car insurance payment options: Option A charges \$48 per fortnight, while Option B charges \$102 per month. Convert both options to annual amounts to determine which is cheaper and calculate the annual saving.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Option A annual cost} = \$48 \times 26 = \$1248$
$\text{Option B annual cost} = \$102 \times 12 = \$1224$
$\text{Annual saving} = \$1248 - \$1224 = \$24$
$\text{Option B is cheaper by \$24 per year.}$

development.question_text: Jack earns \$920 per week. His regular expenses are: Rent \$340/week, Groceries \$160/week, Car insurance \$130/month, Electricity \$390/quarter ($4$ quarters/year), and Entertainment \$150/fortnight. Calculate Jack's annual budget balance and determine his annual savings.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Annual income} = \$920 \times 52 = \$47\,840$
$\text{Rent} = \$340 \times 52 = \$17\,680$
$\text{Groceries} = \$160 \times 52 = \$8320$
$\text{Car insurance} = \$130 \times 12 = \$1560$
$\text{Electricity} = \$390 \times 4 = \$1560$
$\text{Entertainment} = \$150 \times 26 = \$3900$
$\text{Total annual expenses} = \$17\,680 + \$8320 + \$1560 + \$1560 + \$3900 = \$33\,020$
$\text{Annual balance} = \$47\,840 - \$33\,020$
$= \$14\,820\text{ savings}$

$\text{Rent} = \$320 \times 52 = \$16\,640$
$\text{Car Loan} = \$450 \times 12 = \$5400$
$\text{Groceries} = \$260 \times 26 = \$6760$
$\text{Utilities} = \$220 \times 12 = \$2640$
$\text{Recreation} = \$90 \times 52 = \$4680$

$\text{Budget balance} = \$48\,100 - \$36\,120$

development.question_text: Chloe's budget produces a regular surplus of \$175 per week. She is saving for a used car that costs \$7000. How many weeks of saving are required to reach her target?

Lucas earns \$48 000 net per year. His current annual expenses total \$44 400 (Fixed: \$30 000, Discretionary: \$14 400). Lucas sets a goal to save \$7200 per year towards a home deposit. By how much must he reduce his monthly discretionary spending to achieve this savings target?
development.solution_text:
$\text{Target total expenses} = \$48\,000 - \$7200 = \$40\,800$
$\text{Target discretionary expenses} = \$40\,800 - \$30\,000 = \$10\,800$
$\text{Annual reduction required} = \$14\,400 - \$10\,800 = \$3600$
$\text{Monthly reduction} = \dfrac{\$3600}{12}$
$= \$300\text{ per month}$

mastery.question_text: A dual-income household earns \$1150 per week and \$2400 per fortnight. Their annual fixed expenses total \$48 500, and their discretionary expenses are \$650 per fortnight. In addition, they allocate $10\%$ of their total gross annual income into a dedicated retirement investment. Calculate their net annual budget balance.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Income 1} = \$1150 \times 52 = \$59\,800$
$\text{Income 2} = \$2400 \times 26 = \$62\,400$
$\text{Total annual income} = \$59\,800 + \$62\,400 = \$122\,200$
$\text{Retirement investment} = 0.10 \times \$122\,200 = \$12\,220$
$\text{Discretionary expenses} = \$650 \times 26 = \$16\,900$
$\text{Total annual expenses} = \$48\,500 + \$16\,900 + \$12\,220 = \$77\,620$
$\text{Net annual balance} = \$122\,200 - \$77\,620$
$= \$44\,580\text{ surplus}$

mastery.question_text: A university student works part-time, earning \$520 per week during the $36$ academic term weeks and \$900 per week during the $16$ holiday weeks. Her annual fixed expenses are \$21 000. What is the maximum average weekly discretionary spending she can afford across the entire $52$-week year to finish the year with an annual savings surplus of \$3500?
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Total annual income} = (36 \times \$520) + (16 \times \$900) = \$18\,720 + \$14\,400 = \$33\,120$
$\text{Max total expenses} = \$33\,120 - \$3500 = \$29\,620$
$\text{Max discretionary spending} = \$29\,620 - \$21\,000 = \$8620$
$\text{Weekly discretionary budget} = \dfrac{\$8620}{52}$
$\approx \$165.77\text{ per week}$
